title: Does translating your Steam page help during Next Fest? Pages in 10+ languages grew a bit faster, pages with Chinese a lot faster!
author: Dream_Ep
selftext:
While digging into the last Next Fest I kept bumping into languages, so here’s a standalone one

31% of the games on the official list had an English only page. The median small game (under 50 followers) had 3 languages, games between 500 and 10K had 8 (maybe there is a correlation?)

I compared follower growth during the fest (Oct 19 to Oct 29), only between games of the same size, meaning the same number of Steam followers before the fest  


Under 50 followers: 1 language +32%, 2 to 4 +31%, 5 to 9 +42%, 10+ +40%

50 to 499: +18%, +17%, +17%, then +21% at 10+

500 to 10K: +8%, +8%, +10%, +14%



So there’s a slight bump once you go past 4 languages, but honestly it’s small and not even consistent. Between 50 and 499 it only shows up at 10+. Not a magic switch at all hah :D

Chinese is where it shows the most. Pages with Chinese grew +41% vs +30% under 50 followers, and +13% vs +8% between 500 and 10K. Between 50 and 499 it’s almost a tie (+19% vs +17%). That gap is bigger than anything the number of languages does on its own

And that’s where I’m skeptical of my own numbers. A page with Chinese is often a Chinese studio, with its own audience and communities. And maybe it’s mostly those studios that ship a long list of languages in the first place. If that’s true, part of the “more languages” effect could just be the “Chinese studio” effect in disguise. I can’t separate the two with public data

Which leaves the question I actually care about:   
Can a non Chinese game reach Chinese players just by translating? Or do you also need the communities, the streamers, the local platforms? If you’ve added Chinese to your page as a non Chinese dev, I’d love to hear if it changed anything !? :)

So don’t read this as “add Chinese and get 10% more”.  
More like: Chinese players are a big chunk of Next Fest, English only pages don’t talk to them, and a translation alone might not be enough either..!

I’m building NextWishlist, a tool that tracks this kind of stuff for your own game and its niche every day. Link in the comments if you’re curious still free and in private beta!
